findings.title: Debug logging leaks authentication result to server logs
findings.source_evidence: server/index.js:2582: console.error('[DEBUG LOGIN] authenticateAdmin result:', admin);
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: admin session data (role, branch, userId) written to stderr; readable by anyone with access to server logs (Render logs, container logs, log aggregators)
findings.observed_result: The full authenticateAdmin return object — including role, branch, userId, and ok status — is logged to console.error on every login attempt, both success and failure. In production (Render), these logs are retained and accessible to platform operators and potentially to log aggregation services.
findings.safe_reproduction: Static analysis: the console.error call at index.js:2582 logs the `admin` object unconditionally after authenticateAdmin returns. No dynamic execution needed — source path is definitive.
findings.smallest_effective_fix: Remove line 2582 (`console.error('[DEBUG LOGIN] authenticateAdmin result:', admin);`) from server/index.js. If observability is needed, log only a static message without the admin object.
findings.regression_test: Add a test that asserts no console.error call includes the authenticateAdmin result object during login.

findings.title: Debug authorization data leaked in API response and response header
findings.source_evidence: server/index.js:4004-4014: console.error('[DEBUG-PRODUCTS] CHECK:', checkResult); res.status(403).json({ error: ..., test: 'REJECTED-v2', debug: checkResult }); res.setHeader('X-Debug-Check', JSON.stringify(checkResult));
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: Internal branch authorization check data (isBranchAdmin, bodyBranch, adminBranch, different) returned to clients in 403 responses and X-Debug-Check response header on every POST /api/admin/products response
findings.observed_result: When a branch_admin attempts to create a product in a different branch, the 403 response includes a `debug` field containing the full checkResult object. Additionally, every response from this endpoint sets an X-Debug-Check header with the same data. This reveals internal authorization logic to clients.
findings.safe_reproduction: Static analysis: lines 4004-4014 unconditionally include debug data in responses and headers. Source path is definitive.
findings.smallest_effective_fix: 1) Remove the `debug: checkResult` field from the 403 JSON response (line 4007). 2) Remove the `res.setHeader('X-Debug-Check', ...)` call (line 4014). 3) Remove or replace the console.error debug logging (lines 4004-4006) with non-data-leaking logs.
findings.regression_test: Add a test that POSTs to /api/admin/products as branch_admin with a different branch and asserts the response body does not contain a `debug` field and no `X-Debug-Check` header is set.
findings.fixed_in: server/index.js:4004-4014 (removed debug logging, debug field, and X-Debug-Check header) + test/auth.test.js

findings.title: Hardcoded default admin password fallback
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: Superadmin account (ADMIN_USER/ADMIN_PASSWORD). If ADMIN_PASSWORD is not set in the environment, the fallback 'fusionwok' is used, which is also documented in .env.example and README.md.
findings.observed_result: The code falls back to the hardcoded password 'fusionwok' when ADMIN_PASSWORD env var is absent. While validateConfig() in server/config.js rejects this in production (fatal), the fallback still exists in the code path and could be used if config validation is bypassed or in non-production deployments where the check is only a warning.
findings.safe_reproduction: Static analysis: line 183 shows `|| 'fusionwok'` fallback. validateConfig() at config.js:162-167 flags `password === 'fusionwok'` as a problem in production but only a warning in development.
findings.smallest_effective_fix: Remove the `|| 'fusionwok'` fallback from line 183. ADMIN_PASSWORD must be explicitly set; if absent, the superadmin login should fail (not fall back to a predictable default).
findings.regression_test: Add a test that authenticateAdmin returns { ok: false } when ADMIN_PASSWORD is undefined or empty (no fallback).
